info.title: CleanSheets Backend
info.description: Bridge between the CleanSheets iOS app, Google Sheets, Enable Banking, and Supabase. Sign in once at `POST /api/auth/session` with a Google **or** Apple identity token; it returns a backend **access token** (1 h) and a **refresh token** (60 days, single-use). Every other endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` unless noted — identity is resolved from that token to a stable internal user, never from a request body. Sign in with Google at the top of this page to auto-authorize Try-it-out requests (the button mints a Google ID token, exchanges it for a session, and attaches the access token; an Apple token can be pasted into the Authorize dialog's identityToken field and exchanged manually).

accessToken.description: Backend access token from POST /api/auth/session (or /api/auth/session/refresh). Short-lived (1 h) and verified locally; it carries the stable internal user id. This is the credential for every endpoint except the two session endpoints.

identityToken.description: Provider identity token — a Google ID token (audience = GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID) or an Apple identity token (audience = APPLE_CLIENT_ID). Accepted **only** by POST /api/auth/session, which verifies it once and exchanges it for a session.

SessionTokens.description: A backend session. Returned by sign-in and by refresh; the refresh response omits userId/provider (they are unchanged).

accessToken.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` on every other endpoint.

refreshToken.description: Single-use, ~60 days. Store it in the keychain; each refresh returns a replacement.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until accessToken expires (3600). Refresh before this elapses.

userId.description: Stable internal user id (uuid). Sign-in only.

provider.description: Login provider of the verified identity token. Sign-in only.

SpreadsheetList.description: The connected Google account's spreadsheets, most recently modified first.

account.description: E-mail of the Google account the Sheets consent was granted for. Decoupled from the login account (an Apple login connects whichever Google account owns the budget), so the app shows it to answer "which account is this?". Null if Drive reports none.

id.description: Google Sheet ID — send as `sheetId` to POST /api/user/config.

modifiedTime.description: RFC 3339 at whole-second precision (Drive's milliseconds are truncated — the generated Swift client's default date transcoder rejects fractional seconds). The list is ordered by this, newest first.

id.description: Bank-assigned transaction id (Enable Banking entry_reference). Not unique across split transaction lines — dedup uses the composite key id+amount+date (see POST /api/sheet/save)

amount.description: Always positive — direction carries the sign

direction.description: debit = money out (spend), credit = money in (income/refund)

status.description: pending = reserved at the bank, not yet settled — shown instantly so the user recognizes the purchase; amount (and rarely id) can still change when it books

logTabMissing.description: true when the sheet has no _log tab — nothing was filtered out; the app should warn the user

amount.description: Amount to add to the Actual cell. Negative allowed so a refund can reduce the total.

date.description: The queue entry's `date` — part of the composite dedup key

status.description: The queue entry's `status` at save time — decides how the dedup key matches later (booked: id+amount+date, pending: id only)

name.description: New category name. Names the sheet scanners treat as structure (a "Total…" prefix, a section name) are rejected — such a row would be invisible to future saves.

budget.description: Optional Budget value for the new row (written to the section's Budget column)

transactionId.description: The queue entry's `id`. Provide together with `amount`, `date` and `status` to categorize the transaction to the new category in the same request.

amount.description: Amount written to the new row's Actual cell. Negative allowed so a refund can reduce the total.

date.description: The queue entry's `date` — part of the composite dedup key

status.description: The queue entry's `status` at save time — decides how the dedup key matches later (booked: id+amount+date, pending: id only)

row.description: 1-based sheet row of the new category

cell.description: Actual cell written — only when a transaction was categorized

newActual.description: Actual value after the write — only when a transaction was categorized

sections.description: Every section in the stored column mapping that exists on this tab, in mapping order

budget.description: null when the cell is blank/non-numeric or the section has no Budget column mapped

totals.description: Sum of this section's categories (null cells count as 0)
Grand totals across expense sections — every mapped section except Income. Feeds the "Spent this month" card.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired access token — refresh the session (POST /api/auth/session/refresh) and retry, or sign in again

post.summary: Sign in — exchange a provider identity token for a backend session
post.description:
The one place a provider identity token is accepted. Send `Authorization: Bearer <identity_token>` (a Google ID token or an Apple identity token); it is verified once — signature, issuer, audience, expiry — the internal user row is provisioned on first sign-in, and a session token pair is returned. Every other endpoint then takes the returned `accessToken` as Bearer.

This exists because an Apple identity token expires in ~10 minutes and cannot be refreshed on-device: re-verifying it per request would log Sign-in-with-Apple users out constantly.

200.description: Signed in — store both tokens (the refresh token in the keychain)

401.description: Missing or invalid identity token — run native sign-in again

post.summary: Refresh the session — swap a refresh token for a fresh pair
post.description: Unauthenticated by design: the refresh token *is* the credential, and the access token it replaces has usually expired. **The refresh token is single-use** — the presented one is consumed and a new pair returned (rotation), so the response must be stored before the next call. On 401 the session is over (unknown, expired, already used, or the account was deleted) and the app must run native sign-in again.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token from the last session response

200.description: New token pair — replaces the old one

401.description: `SESSION_EXPIRED` — the refresh token is unknown, expired or already used; sign in again

example.message: Session expired or already refreshed — sign in again

post.summary: Setup state — what the signed-in caller still has to connect
post.description: Reports the caller's setup state after sign-in. Despite the name it works for Apple-login users too; sign-in itself (and user-row provisioning) happens at POST /api/auth/session, so this takes the access token like every other endpoint.

provider.description: Login provider of the verified token

hasConfig.description: true when a sheet_id is saved

hasSheetsAccess.description: true when a Sheets-scope refresh token is stored

get.summary: Start the Google Sheets consent flow (action=start)
get.description: Returns the Google consent URL that grants the backend a Sheets-scope refresh token. Open the returned URL in a browser. The callback (`/auth/google/callback`) is browser-only and not testable here — it no longer stores the refresh token; it redirects to `cleansheets://oauth/google?status=success&handle=<handle>` with a one-time, ~2-minute handle, and the app completes the connection with POST /api/auth/google/finalize.

post.summary: Finalize Google Sheets access under the authenticated caller
post.description: Second step of the Google Sheets connect flow (task 17). The browser callback no longer stores the refresh token; it redirects to `cleansheets://oauth/google?status=success&handle=<handle>` with a one-time, ~2-minute handle. The app calls this endpoint with that handle and its own access token, and the refresh token is stored under the verified caller — so a consent completed against someone else's flow can never attach Google Sheets access to a stranger's account. The handle is single-use and must belong to the same account that started the flow.

handle.description: One-time handle from the callback deep link

400.description: Invalid body, or the handle expired before finalize

403.description: Handle belongs to a different account

get.summary: Start the Enable Banking consent flow
get.description: Returns the bank authorization URL (MitID in production, instant approval at Mock ASPSP in sandbox). Open the returned URL in a browser. In sandbox `bank`/`country` default to the Mock ASPSP; in production both are required. The callback (`/auth/bank/callback`) is browser-only and not testable here — it redirects to `cleansheets://oauth/bank?status=success&handle=<handle>`, and the app completes the connection with POST /api/auth/bank/finalize.

parameters.name: bank
parameters.description: ASPSP name as listed by Enable Banking, e.g. "Nordea"

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter ISO country code of the bank

400.description: Missing/invalid bank selection or bank rejected the request

500.description: Server configuration, credential, or storage failure — message names the failing step

get.summary: Bank consent health for the Settings screen
get.description: Reports the caller's Enable Banking consent state from the stored expiry: `expired` once the expiry has passed (or no bank was ever connected — `expiresAt` is null then), `expiring` within 14 days of expiry, otherwise `healthy`. `renewAvailable` is true whenever the consent is expiring or expired, i.e. the app should offer the (re)connect button. Renewing is the normal connect flow: GET /api/auth/bank and open the returned URL.

expiresAt.description: Consent expiry (`valid_until`) at whole-second precision (a stored value's milliseconds are truncated — the generated Swift client's default date transcoder rejects fractional seconds); null when no bank connection is stored

post.summary: Finalize a bank connection under the authenticated caller
post.description: Second step of the connect flow (task 15). The browser callback no longer stores the bank session; it redirects to `cleansheets://oauth/bank?status=success&handle=<handle>` with a one-time, ~2-minute handle. The app calls this endpoint with that handle and its own access token, and the session is stored under the verified caller — so a consent completed against someone else's flow can never attach to a stranger's account. The handle is single-use and must belong to the same account that started the flow.

handle.description: One-time handle from the callback deep link

expiresAt.description: Consent expiry (`valid_until`) at whole-second precision, as on GET /api/auth/bank/status

400.description: Invalid body, or the handle expired before finalize

403.description: Handle belongs to a different account

get.summary: Fetch uncategorized bank transactions, newest first
get.description: Fetches booked and pending (reserved) transactions from the last 30 days via the caller's stored Enable Banking session (all consented accounts), filters out entries already saved to the sheet's `_log` tab, and returns the rest newest first. The filter matches `_log` rows saved as booked on the composite key id+amount+date (banks reuse one id across split transaction lines), and rows saved as pending on id alone (a pending transaction can change amount/date when it books). Pending transactions are included so a purchase appears while the user still remembers it; they carry `status: "pending"`. Returns `BANK_TOKEN_EXPIRED` when the bank consent is missing, expired, or revoked — sessions cannot be refreshed, the user must reconnect. A missing `_log` tab is not an error: nothing is filtered and `logTabMissing` is true so the app can warn.

401.description: `GOOGLE_TOKEN_EXPIRED` (missing/invalid ID token) or `BANK_TOKEN_EXPIRED` (bank consent missing, expired, or revoked — reconnect)

404.description: No sheet configured yet, or the configured sheet is not accessible

500.description: Server configuration, credential, or storage failure — message names the failing step

post.summary: Categorize a transaction — add its amount to the category's Actual cell
post.description: Finds the current month tab (by English month name, e.g. "July"), locates the section+category row via the caller's stored column mapping (defaults F/H), and adds `amount` to the Actual cell. A `_log` row (transactionId, section, category, amount, date, status, savedAt) is written BEFORE the Actual cell — crash-safety per product spec §7b: if the Actual write fails, the log entry blocks a retry from double-counting. The hidden `_log` tab is created on first save. Duplicates are rejected with 409: booked saves match on id+amount+date (split lines with a shared id stay saveable), pending saves on id alone. The Left column is never written to.

200.description: Saved — new Actual value and the row written

404.description: `SHEET_NOT_FOUND` (no sheet configured, sheet/month tab not accessible) or `CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND` (no row for section+category)

500.description: `SHEET_WRITE_FAILED` (a write failed — if the `_log` row was already written, retrying returns 409 and the Actual cell was not changed) or `SUPABASE_ERROR`

delete.summary: Undo a save — reverse the Actual write and remove the _log entry
delete.description: Finds the newest `_log` row for `transactionId` (split lines share an id; undo follows immediately after a save), subtracts its logged amount from the section+category Actual cell of the current month tab, then deletes the `_log` row so the transaction returns to the queue. Operates only on the verified caller's own sheet (their stored config and Google consent).

200.description: Undone — new Actual value and the row reversed

404.description: No `_log` entry for this transactionId (`INVALID_REQUEST`), or sheet/month tab/category row not found (`SHEET_NOT_FOUND` / `CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND`)

409.description: The `_log` entry is incomplete (legacy row) and cannot be reversed (`INVALID_REQUEST`)

post.summary: Create a new category row — optionally categorize a transaction to it in one step
post.description: Creates a new category in the `section` box of the current month tab by writing `name` (and the optional `budget`) into the box's first empty row — the spare formatted rows above the section's Total. Nothing is inserted or shifted, so the dashboard layout, formatting, and Total formulas are untouched; the Left column is never written to. A duplicate category name in the section is rejected with 409, as is a box with no empty row left (add one in the sheet first). When `transactionId` + `amount` + `date` + `status` are provided, the transaction is saved to the new category in the same request with the exact `/api/sheet/save` semantics: the dedup gate runs BEFORE the row is written (an already-saved transaction leaves no orphan category), and the `_log` entry is written before the Actual cell (crash-safety per product spec §7b). If the request dies after the name was written, retrying returns 409 (duplicate category) — save the transaction via POST /api/sheet/save instead.

200.description: Created — the new row, plus the Actual cell and value when a transaction was categorized

400.description: Validation failed (`INVALID_REQUEST`) — bad body, save fields not provided together, name conflicts with sheet structure, or no Budget column mapped while `budget` was given

404.description: `SHEET_NOT_FOUND` (no sheet configured, sheet/month tab not accessible) or `CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND` (section box not found in the tab)

409.description: Category already exists in the section, the section has no empty row left, or the transaction was already saved (`INVALID_REQUEST`)

get.summary: List the connected Google account's spreadsheets
get.description:
Populates the app's onboarding sheet picker. Lists spreadsheets the caller's **connected Google account** can open — most recently modified first, one bounded page, trashed files excluded — plus that account's e-mail. Takes no parameters: the Drive is whichever one the stored consent belongs to.

Needs the `drive.metadata.readonly` scope, added to the consent in task 22. A refresh token granted **before** that (or a revoked one) answers `401 GOOGLE_TOKEN_EXPIRED` — re-run the Google Sheets consent; a grant cannot gain a scope it was never given.

500.description: Google Drive could not be reached (including: the Drive API is not enabled on the Google project)

get.summary: List tabs, or scan one tab's sections/categories/columns
get.description: Without `tab`: returns the spreadsheet's tab names. With `tab`: scans the tab and returns detected sections, their categories (with Budget/Actual values), and column positions. Opens the sheet with the caller's stored Sheets consent — a sheet the account cannot access returns `SHEET_NOT_FOUND`; missing/expired consent returns `GOOGLE_TOKEN_EXPIRED`.

parameters.name: sheetId
parameters.description: Google Sheet ID (from the sheet URL)

parameters.name: tab
parameters.description: Tab name to scan, e.g. "July". Omit to list tabs.

200.description: Tab list (no `tab` param) or detected structure (`tab` given)

404.description: Sheet or tab not found, or not accessible to this Google account

get.summary: Budget overview — Budget/Actual per category with section and grand totals
get.description: Reads the caller's configured sheet and returns every mapped section found on the tab, each with its categories' Budget/Actual values and section totals. The top-level `totals` sum the expense sections only (every mapped section except `Income`) — they feed the app's "Spent this month" card. Sections are located via the stored column mapping, so the overview lists exactly the categories a save can write to; a mapped section missing from the tab is skipped. Without `tab`, the current month's tab is used (`SHEET_NOT_FOUND` when no tab is named after the current month).

parameters.name: tab
parameters.description: Tab name to read, e.g. "July". Defaults to the current month's tab.

404.description: No sheet configured yet, unknown tab, no tab for the current month, or sheet not accessible

200.description: Current config (fields are null until saved)

post.summary: Save sheet ID and/or column mapping

delete.summary: Delete the caller's account and all backend-stored data
delete.description: Permanently deletes everything CleanSheets stores for the verified caller: their `users` row (config + encrypted Google/bank tokens) and any in-flight pending grants (`bank_pending_sessions`, `google_pending_grants`) they started. Before deleting, it best-effort-revokes the external grants — the Google refresh token (`POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke`) and the Enable Banking session (`DELETE /sessions/{id}`); a revocation failure is logged but does not fail the deletion. Identity comes only from the verified token, so only the caller's own data is affected. **The user's Google Sheet (including its `_log` tab) is deliberately left untouched — it is their own document.** Idempotent: deleting an already-deleted account returns 200. Implements App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v) (in-app account deletion).

note.description: Confirms the user's Google Sheet was left untouched.
